pool_policy_revision.b0_impact: none - the rule reproduces 150 at 25/s, so every B0 cell and every W2/W3/W4 cell is pool-identical
pool_policy_revision.change: generator pool is derived from rate x timeout with 10% headroom, rounded up to 50
pool_policy_revision.decided_by: owner instruction to raise the pool when the limit is a framework artifact rather than a platform limit
evidence: ThingsBoard qualification w1-qual-tb-20261110c recorded implied_in_flight_at_p99 = 243 against a 150 pool
the same run needed ~11 VUs in measurement once warm, and dropped nothing there
FIWARE qualification w1-qual-fw-20261110c dropped only during a 30 s latency stall, not at steady state
B0 peak was 125 (ThingsBoard) and 16 (FIWARE) at 25/s, so the 150 cap never bound any B0 cell
pool_policy_revision.not_claimed: This is not a platform capacity claim and does not authorize a throughput claim above the fixed points.
pool_policy_revision.scope: generator concurrency only; no platform-side resource or deployment setting changes
pool_policy_revision.w1_impact: W1 50/s moves 150 -> 300; this is the pool W1 always required (rate x timeout = 250)
